citations.quote: There is no such tie to NAV for the CEF, leading to a more persistent discount or premium.
That seems cheap; however, very few events will cause that discount to narrow dramatically.
This arbitrage opportunity not only creates an incentive for APs to provide liquidity but also keeps the ETF trading at or near fair value.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: ETF and CEF prices both float free of NAV, but the deviations mean opposite things: an ETF's premium/discount is transient noise that the AP creation/redemption channel collapses, while a CEF's lacks any such tie and stays persistent, so a wide CEF discount is not automatically cheap.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: ETF vs Closed-End-Fund Premium/Discount: Transient vs Persistent
